title: Orsen and the Static
premise: Coral Thornbury has spent a decade alone tending Earth's abandoned seed vault, running supply routes between colonies that severed contact after the Static War began. When a derelict ship returns from deep space carrying its crew aged backward into childhood, Coral discovers they hold a message from the war's origin that could end it — or hand one side the weapon that started everything. Hunted by both fleets and racing the crew's fading, regressing memories, Coral must choose between delivering the truth and protecting the child who once was the person she loved. In the end, Coral broadcasts the message to all sides at once, ending the war at the cost of her own memories of why she ever stayed.
about_author: Lior Thornbury is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent years cataloguing transmissions nobody claimed. They write science fiction about people who keep things running after everyone else stops caring.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishes her solitary life ferrying seeds and supplies between silent colony stations, her ritual of reading old letters aloud to the vault's dormant stacks. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into routine, and the ache of a name she won't say.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Coral intercepts a distress ping from the Meridian, a deep-space vessel lost eleven years ago. Boarding the drifting hull, she finds the crew alive — but aged backward into children who don't know her, except one boy who flinches at her voice. POV: Coral. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Coral cares for the regressed crew aboard her hauler, learning their captain is now eight years old and the boy, Ede, keeps drawing the same antenna array in crayon. A military patrol hails her; she lies for the first time in ten years. POV: Coral. Beat: protective love awakening against duty.

chapters.title: What the Antenna Remembers
chapters.summary: Ede's drawings lead Coral to an encrypted core in the Meridian's hold: a recording proving the first Static strike was fired by the fleet now claiming self-defense. The children begin forgetting faster near the core, as if it feeds on them. POV: alternating Coral and fragments of adult Ede's logs. Beat: the truth as burden.

chapters.title: Both Flags
chapters.summary: Two warships — one from each side — converge on Coral's position, each offering sanctuary and demanding the core. She plays them against each other and slips away through a debris field, losing half her cargo and nearly a child. POV: Coral. Beat: power revealed as appetite on every side.

chapters.title: Ede
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: while hiding in a dead station, Coral reads Ede her own unsent letters, and the boy remembers pieces of the man he was — her partner, lost with the Meridian. He asks her not to let him forget again. POV: Coral. Beat: love against duty made intimate and unbearable.

chapters.title: The Vault's Last Seed
chapters.summary: Cornered, Coral returns to Earth's seed vault, intending to hide the core among the archives. Instead she finds a fleet strike team already there, harvesting the vault itself for bio-weapons research. She triggers the vault's lockdown, sealing herself in with the truth. POV: Coral. Beat: betrayal of everything sacred by those sworn to protect it.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Inside the sealed vault, the core fully activates, and Coral experiences the original attack through the regressed crew's residual memories — including Ede's final adult act: stealing the evidence to bring home. Both fleets breach the vault doors simultaneously. POV: Coral within shared memory. Beat: climax begins; memory as battlefield.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Coral hijacks the vault's planetary transmitter and plays the unedited recording to every world at once, refusing both fleets' demands to surrender it. The fleets open fire on the vault — and on each other — as colonies rise in refusal across the network. Ede, nearly forgotten entirely, holds her hand. POV: Coral. Beat: sacrifice as choice, not defeat.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Weeks later, under a fragile ceasefire, Coral tends the damaged vault with the recovering crew, whose memories return slowly and incompletely. Ede, now aging forward again, doesn't remember loving her — but stays anyway, planting the first restored seed row. POV: Coral. Beat: bittersweet resolution; what remains when memory fails is what we choose next.
